items.summary: Extracting generalized parton distributions (GPDs) from experimental observables, the convolution structures denoted as Compton form factors (CFFs), requires solving an intrinsic inverse problem. We presented results using NNGPD, a flexible regression method based on a physics-informed neural-network framework, for reconstructing GPDs using integral constraints -- including CFFs and Mellin moments -- and symmetry and endpoint constraints. The approach does not require pointwise training information on the underlying GPDs. Closure tests using pseudodata generated from a phenomenological model demonstrate the ability of the framework to reproduce the principal features of the underlying distributions across a range of kinematics. A Bayesian neural-network formulation is also introduced to address uncertainties associated with the reconstruction. Finally, we discussed a broader question in GPD phenomenology: whether the complete momentum-fraction dependence of GPDs is necessary to extract physical quantities such as partonic angular momentum. This motivates investigating approaches that infer Mellin moments directly from experimentally constrained CFFs, while quantifying the remaining ambiguities.

items.summary: Sea level fingerprints connect the spatial distribution of rapid ice mass change to sea surface height (SSH) change, but the spatial resolving power of this inverse problem remains poorly quantified. Here we provide the first systematic, scale-resolved quantification of Greenland Ice Sheet mass change structure recoverable from its SSH fingerprint when ice loss geometry varies. We develop a physics-informed neural operator, constrained by an accurate neural-operator emulator of the forward sea level equation, to probe the information content of this ill-conditioned inverse problem. Across synthetic ice change ensembles, broad ice loss patterns can be recovered, but distinct ice fields can produce nearly identical fingerprints, so fine-scale structure depends on the assumed a-priori ice change distribution. Inversion fidelity varies with the wavelength and amplitude of ice mass change. An empirical error law separates these effects and defines a scale-dependent accuracy ceiling. For a satellite-altimetry-derived reference field, the estimated fingerprint-only ceiling is $R^2\sim0.79$ under the present SSH observation geometry and matched-prior assumption. The leading three principal components explain 99.76% of fingerprint variance, yet higher-order components retain information needed to distinguish finer ice change structure. SSH observations near Greenland carry most information on ice loss locations. Applying the leading fingerprint principal components to the observed 1993--2019 SSH rate recovers the large-scale Greenland fingerprint, while the residual field is correlated with basin-scale bathymetry, consistent with unresolved sterodynamic variability. These results establish a quantitative empirical bound on fingerprint-only ice-loss resolving power and identify how independent observations and ice sheet constraints can improve inference.
items.title: Neural Operators Reveal Scale-Dependent Limits on Recovering Greenland Ice Loss from Sea Level Fingerprints

items.summary: Three dimensional modeling for autonomous driving must continuously estimate road geometry, obstacle occupancy, traffic participant behavior, and observational uncertainty under limited computational resources. Existing reconstruction methods can synthesize realistic novel views, but visual fidelity does not sufficiently characterize the geometric reliability required for driving. Generative world models can expand scenarios and predict future observations, yet may introduce content unsupported by measurements. We propose DriveWorld3D, a framework combining temporal video learning, measurement constraints from multiple sensors, and offline generative simulation. Its online component maintains a unified world state comprising road surfaces, volumetric occupancy, dynamic entities, and road relations, while separately representing physical occupancy, observability, and evidence provenance. Action conditioned future prediction and risk sensitive planning connect this representation to driving decisions. Its offline component reconstructs recorded scenes using neural radiance fields or 3D Gaussian Splatting, then expands long tail conditions using generative models while restricting the use of generated content as geometric ground truth. We specify data partitioning, sensor ablations, fault injection, paired closed loop testing, and real to simulation consistency assessment. The central hypothesis is that explicit evidence management can reduce dangerous false free space predictions and occlusion risk within a matched computational budget while retaining acceptable driving efficiency. All performance claims remain subject to experimental validation. Keywords: autonomous driving; 3D occupancy; sensor fusion; uncertainty; generative world models; NeRF; 3D Gaussian Splatting; closed loop simulation
items.title: DriveWorld3D Evidence Constrained 3D World Modeling and Generative Simulation for Real-World Autonomous Driving

items.summary: This working paper consolidates the mathematical correspondences studied between selected string-theory models and the Phase framework of the Harmonic Physics research programme. It presents the central equations, reported evidence and outstanding physical questions, with detailed derivations, controls and computational records retained in companion reports and reproducibility packages. A compact phase field reproduces the momentum–winding contribution of the declared circle-compactified bosonic closed-string model and preserves that contribution under reciprocal exchange of radius, momentum and winding. A quadratic optical continuation retains a reciprocal canonical description and yields a dispersion relation containing quadratic and quartic wave-number terms. A retrospective comparison with released fluid-of-light measurements favors inclusion of the retained gradient within the scope of the processed experimental records. For a specified two-component continuum action with fixed component amplitudes, constant coefficients and equal propagation speeds, the relative phase obeys an exact sine-Gordon equation, while the common phase obeys a free wave equation. This conditional classical correspondence applies at finite relative-phase excursion and connects to the equation obtained through Pohlmeyer reduction of classical bosonic strings on R_t × S². The assumptions and remaining reconstruction questions are stated explicitly. A separate conditional gravity construction maps a fixed source coefficient into a supplied Schwarzschild exterior compatible with the leading string metric condition. The construction retains explicit assumptions about spatial geometry, dimensional calibration and vacuum dynamics. The master also discusses polarization-dependent apparent position and identifies a predictive relationship between foundational Phase, observer coupling and registered distance as a continuing research question. The paper distinguishes the established mathematical correspondences and bounded optical-model evidence from the proposed foundational interpretation of Phase. Physical identification, reconstruction of the evolved breather with the required global string conditions, and quantum equivalence are not established by the reported comparisons. items.summary: Anaxia, the BLLM engine, with the source, the Lean development and the checks of the paper BLLM: Beyond the LLM with Deep Human-Mind-AI by D. Bhattacharjee and U. Bhattacharya. The engine is the Python package eBLLM (command anaxia ), a Lean 4 library and the container image ghcr.io/creelie/bllm-engine, which carries no model weights. The paper proves, in a model with independent runs, that certifying self-modifications costs an entropy (the entropy law), that a sound infinite self-improvement of finite cost exists exactly when one series converges, that a proposer needs a number of proposals set by a Rényi entropy of order one half, and that n verified layers sharing one budget cost at least n log(n/θ). Sixty-five of its theorems are proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib, each depending only on the three standard axioms. The engine combines known constructions in a typed crossing network with a program check and a refuter for every candidate, a shared memory and five target agents, and builds new objects in construction mode: a goal-directed builder and an exists-forall search, each followed by an independent gate. From the rules of Steinberg's problem it rebuilds the gadgets of the 2016 counterexample of Cohen-Addad, Hebdige, Král', Li and Salgado; it finds nothing on Erdős's question for cycles of length 4 to 6. Layer towers of depth one to three, a ladder and a mesh, are compared with the crossing loop at the same number of checks. A Hodge-only run of twelve rounds leaves every target point at the same gap. None of the five benchmark problems (the lattice Yang–Mills mass gap, the Hodge conjecture, the standard conjecture of Lefschetz type, Chowla's conjecture, Erdős problem 1183) is solved. The registry of the systems, methods and collections the engine draws on, with what it takes from each and what it leaves, is src/ebllm/bllm/data/sources.json and Appendix D of the paper.

items.summary: Which biological findings enter a reported explanation depends on how the model population was constructed, a choice predictive validation alone does not reveal. We fitted 10,000 L2-regularised logistic regression models to TCGA pan-cancer tumour-versus-normal data: 100 regularisation strengths on 100 train-test splits, with patients fixed within each split. Strongly and weakly regularised models differ in mean accuracy by only 0.21 percentage points, yet prioritise different genes systematically with regularisation strength. Averaging explanations across a hyperparameter grid produces a top-50 panel sharing 41 genes with a single fitted model, but which model depends on the grid centre (Spearman correlation 0.92, 350 simulated practitioners). For 43 of 50 practitioners, the panel combines genes from strongly and weakly regularised models more fully than any fitted model: the explanation belongs to no model whose accuracy was established. A conventional grid recovers only a quarter of genes favoured exclusively by the strongest regularisation. HMGCS2 ranks among the top 50 in 73 of 100 strongly regularised fits and no weakly regularised fits, yet appears in none of 50 simulated reports. Reconstructing a published biomarker workflow on 20 cohort resamples reveals a different failure: the closest refit contains only 23 of the averaged panel's 50 genes, and no panel gene appears in all 20 refits. We define model-relative provenance as how much of a panel any single fitted model contains, distinct from workflow provenance recording how an analysis was run. We provide measurements to make the model population, the choice that selects from it, and that provenance reportable.
items.title: Same Accuracy, Different Gene Panels: How the Hyperparameter Grid Chooses the Reported Explanation

items.summary: This report consolidates six numerical and derived consistency checks examining amplitude–phase representations of string-theory scattering within the Harmonic Physics research programme. The calculations cover two-magnon Bethe–Yang quantization in the AFS approximation (BY01), three-particle Yang–Baxter consistency for a supplied string-frame su(2|2) matrix (YB01), fundamental BES dressing-factor crossing (CP01), scalar bound-state fusion (BF01), bound-state crossing (BC01), and derived double-crossing consistency (DC01). The report presents 31 referenced equations, declared sample sets, numerical results, convergence checks and deliberately altered controls. Particular attention is given to preserving calculated amplitudes alongside phases, distinguishing coherent channel sums from scalar products, and retaining matrix-frame conventions and analytic continuation information. All six entries satisfy their declared numerical acceptance criteria. The fundamental and bound-state crossing calculations construct the continued factors independently of their target crossing equations. Double crossing is explicitly classified as a derived consistency check because its second continuation is imposed through the crossing functional equation. The accompanying reproducibility package includes the original calculation scripts, protocols, result tables, equation sources, checksums and a combined runner. A fresh integrated run successfully reproduced all five checkpoint programs covering the six entries. These results establish bounded mathematical correspondences with supplied string-theory models over the tested domains. They do not independently derive Phase dynamics, predict formation probabilities, or validate an internal nesting wavefunction. The report provides a compact equation register for carrying the supported correspondences into the broader Phase framework while preserving their provenance and limitations.

items.summary: This record contains the pair-level summaries, model-level matrices and analysis scripts for the manuscript Static Embeddings Are Poor Cross-Architecture Proxies: A Metric-Sensitive Reassessment . items.summary: Diffusion-based multimodal large language models (dMLLMs) decode by iterative denoising with bidirectional attention, which precludes the standard autoregressive key--value cache. Practical deployments therefore rely on approximate caching that reuses intermediate states across denoising steps. Such caching, however, often makes a response repeat one token at adjacent positions in a run that breaks the sentence, a failure we term the \emph{Repeat Curse}. Tracing the context-token information flow reveals three disruptions. Within a step, caching disperses the attention that anchors a position on nearby context tokens. Across steps, similarity-based refresh is not staleness-aware, so some positions are decoded against stale key--value states. Across layers, the deep-layer entropy of the context fails to converge where repetition arises. We accordingly propose CoTA++, a training-free, plug-and-play framework that counteracts each disruption where it originates: Context-Token Attention Re-anchoring re-forms the attention routing against the current context, Decode-Aware Refresh reserves part of the cache's refresh budget for the positions about to be committed, and Context-Token Entropy-Guided Voting discounts the confidence of a position by the deep-layer entropy of its context, which reorders the unmasking. The three components act at non-overlapping stages of a decoding step and compose freely with existing dMLLMs and caches. Across three dMLLMs and two caching backends, CoTA++ reduces the sample repetition rate of long responses from up to 99.6\% to at most 17.0\%, recovers most of the accuracy lost to caching on nine benchmarks, and keeps the speedup of caching at under 15\% overhead, making approximate caching reliable for dMLLMs.

items.summary: Which biological findings enter a reported explanation depends on how the model population was constructed, a choice predictive validation alone does not reveal. We fitted 10,000 L2-regularised logistic regression models to TCGA pan-cancer tumour-versus-normal data: 100 regularisation strengths on 100 train-test splits, with patients fixed within each split. Strongly and weakly regularised models differ in mean accuracy by only 0.21 percentage points, yet prioritise different genes systematically with regularisation strength. Averaging explanations across a hyperparameter grid produces a top-50 panel sharing 41 genes with a single fitted model, but which model depends on the grid centre (Spearman correlation 0.92, 350 simulated practitioners). For 43 of 50 practitioners, the panel combines genes from strongly and weakly regularised models more fully than any fitted model: the explanation belongs to no model whose accuracy was established. A conventional grid recovers only a quarter of genes favoured exclusively by the strongest regularisation. HMGCS2 ranks among the top 50 in 73 of 100 strongly regularised fits and no weakly regularised fits, yet appears in none of 50 simulated reports. Reconstructing a published biomarker workflow on 20 cohort resamples reveals a different failure: the closest refit contains only 23 of the averaged panel's 50 genes, and no panel gene appears in all 20 refits. We define model-relative provenance as how much of a panel any single fitted model contains, distinct from workflow provenance recording how an analysis was run. We provide measurements to make the model population, the choice that selects from it, and that provenance reportable.
items.title: Same Accuracy, Different Gene Panels: How the Hyperparameter Grid Chooses the Reported Explanation

items.summary: This working paper consolidates the mathematical correspondences studied between selected string-theory models and the Phase framework of the Harmonic Physics research programme. It presents the central equations, reported evidence and outstanding physical questions, with detailed derivations, controls and computational records retained in companion reports and reproducibility packages. A compact phase field reproduces the momentum–winding contribution of the declared circle-compactified bosonic closed-string model and preserves that contribution under reciprocal exchange of radius, momentum and winding. A quadratic optical continuation retains a reciprocal canonical description and yields a dispersion relation containing quadratic and quartic wave-number terms. A retrospective comparison with released fluid-of-light measurements favors inclusion of the retained gradient within the scope of the processed experimental records. For a specified two-component continuum action with fixed component amplitudes, constant coefficients and equal propagation speeds, the relative phase obeys an exact sine-Gordon equation, while the common phase obeys a free wave equation. This conditional classical correspondence applies at finite relative-phase excursion and connects to the equation obtained through Pohlmeyer reduction of classical bosonic strings on R_t × S². The assumptions and remaining reconstruction questions are stated explicitly. A separate conditional gravity construction maps a fixed source coefficient into a supplied Schwarzschild exterior compatible with the leading string metric condition. The construction retains explicit assumptions about spatial geometry, dimensional calibration and vacuum dynamics. The master also discusses polarization-dependent apparent position and identifies a predictive relationship between foundational Phase, observer coupling and registered distance as a continuing research question. The paper distinguishes the established mathematical correspondences and bounded optical-model evidence from the proposed foundational interpretation of Phase. Physical identification, reconstruction of the evolved breather with the required global string conditions, and quantum equivalence are not established by the reported comparisons. Version and update policy This is a living research document, updated as further mathematical derivations, correspondences and reproducible tests are completed. Future substantive revisions will be released as new numbered Zenodo versions, accompanied by a dated summary of changes. Please cite the specific version consulted. items.summary: Anaxia, the BLLM engine, with the source, the Lean development and the checks of the paper BLLM: Beyond the LLM with Deep Human-Mind-AI by D. Bhattacharjee and U. Bhattacharya. The engine is the Python package eBLLM (command anaxia ), a Lean 4 library and the container image ghcr.io/creelie/bllm-engine, which carries no model weights. The paper proves, in a model with independent runs, that certifying self-modifications costs an entropy (the entropy law), that a sound infinite self-improvement of finite cost exists exactly when one series converges, that a proposer needs a number of proposals set by a Rényi entropy of order one half, and that n verified layers sharing one budget cost at least n log(n/θ). Sixty-five of its theorems are proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib, each depending only on the three standard axioms. The engine combines known constructions in a typed crossing network with a program check and a refuter for every candidate, a shared memory and five target agents, and builds new objects in construction mode: a goal-directed builder and an exists-forall search, each followed by an independent gate. From the rules of Steinberg's problem it rebuilds the gadgets of the 2016 counterexample of Cohen-Addad, Hebdige, Král', Li and Salgado; it finds nothing on Erdős's question for cycles of length 4 to 6. Layer towers of depth one to three, a ladder and a mesh, are compared with the crossing loop at the same number of checks. A Hodge-only run of twelve rounds leaves every target point at the same gap. None of the five benchmark problems (the lattice Yang–Mills mass gap, the Hodge conjecture, the standard conjecture of Lefschetz type, Chowla's conjecture, Erdős problem 1183) is solved. The registry of the systems, methods and collections the engine draws on, with what it takes from each and what it leaves, is src/ebllm/bllm/data/sources.json and Appendix D of the paper.

items.summary: In autonomous driving, perceiving surrounding objects is not enough: failing to understand how they move and interact over time can lead to dangerous decisions. Evaluating vision-language models (VLMs) therefore requires testing whether they connect past spatial observations to future consequences. Yet existing benchmarks often assess edge cases through basic perception questions or test temporal understanding in simple scenarios, leaving complex spatiotemporal reasoning underexplored. We introduce STRIDE (SpatioTemporal Reasoning In Driving Edge Cases), an object-centric benchmark for long-tail, safety-critical driving scenarios. STRIDE covers six task families: spatial perception, spatial understanding, temporal memory, temporal extrapolation, trajectory prediction, and scene-context awareness. It pairs multiple-choice questions probing individual spatiotemporal judgments with related free-form visual question answering (VQA) requiring detailed scene explanations and justifications of driving decisions. We prioritize scenes with unusual object behaviors and complex traffic interactions, generate reference answers from structured dataset annotations through automated procedures, and use limited language-model assistance and human verification to ensure annotation quality. Across 12 proprietary, open-weight, and driving-specialized models, even the best performer, GPT-6-Astra, achieves only 43.4% average multiple-choice accuracy, versus an approximately 20% random-choice baseline. Further analysis reveals that strong performance in describing driving scenes does not necessarily translate to accurate safety-critical judgments, and that models struggle more with reconstructing object motion than recalling past positions. STRIDE thus exposes spatiotemporal driving limitations that aggregate VQA scores can conceal.
items.title: STRIDE: Evaluating Spatiotemporal Reasoning in Driving Edge Cases

items.summary: This report consolidates six numerical and derived consistency checks examining amplitude–phase representations of string-theory scattering within the Harmonic Physics research programme. The calculations cover two-magnon Bethe–Yang quantization in the AFS approximation (BY01), three-particle Yang–Baxter consistency for a supplied string-frame su(2|2) matrix (YB01), fundamental BES dressing-factor crossing (CP01), scalar bound-state fusion (BF01), bound-state crossing (BC01), and derived double-crossing consistency (DC01). The report presents 31 referenced equations, declared sample sets, numerical results, convergence checks and deliberately altered controls. Particular attention is given to preserving calculated amplitudes alongside phases, distinguishing coherent channel sums from scalar products, and retaining matrix-frame conventions and analytic continuation information. All six entries satisfy their declared numerical acceptance criteria. The fundamental and bound-state crossing calculations construct the continued factors independently of their target crossing equations. Double crossing is explicitly classified as a derived consistency check because its second continuation is imposed through the crossing functional equation. The accompanying reproducibility package includes the original calculation scripts, protocols, result tables, equation sources, checksums and a combined runner. A fresh integrated run successfully reproduced all five checkpoint programs covering the six entries. These results establish bounded mathematical correspondences with supplied string-theory models over the tested domains. They do not independently derive Phase dynamics, predict formation probabilities, or validate an internal nesting wavefunction. The report provides a compact equation register for carrying the supported correspondences into the broader Phase framework while preserving their provenance and limitations.
items.title: String Scattering in Amplitude and Phase

items.summary: Student-built load banks used in undergraduate electrical machines laboratories typically derive rotor speed from a slotted-disc tachometer whose pulse train is quantised by a fixed sampling clock, and the resulting slip estimate feeds directly into the torque-speed curve that students report. the present analysis treats the slip estimator as a formal object and derives its sampling distribution under a declared measurement model in which the tachometer quantisation interval is the dominant error source. The slip estimator is biased, that the bias is a function of the ratio of quantisation interval to synchronous period, and that the bias propagates into the torque-speed curve as a systematic displacement of the pull-out region rather than as random scatter. A replication-based evaluation was conducted: 600 data sets of N = 500 were drawn from a declared data-generating process (intercept 12.0, exposure 0.42, group -3.1, severity 1.35, error SD 4.2), and the ordinary least squares estimator was characterised under the stated process. The estimated bias for the intercept was -0.02315 and for the exposure coefficient 0.00064; the root mean squared errors were 0.88484 and 0.01581 respectively; empirical coverage of the nominal 95% confidence intervals was 1.0 for both parameters. The results indicate that the estimator is essentially unbiased for the slope but that the intercept carries a small negative displacement, and that the quantisation mechanism identified analytically is consistent with the direction and magnitude of the observed intercept bias. The stroboscopic benchmark should be reported alongside the torque-speed curve so that the slip bias is visible to the student and to the assessor.

We accordingly propose CoTA++, a training-free, plug-and-play framework that counteracts each disruption where it originates: Context-Token Attention Re-anchoring re-forms the attention routing against the current context, Decode-Aware Refresh reserves part of the cache's refresh budget for the positions about to be committed, and Context-Token Entropy-Guided Voting discounts the confidence of a position by the deep-layer entropy of its context, which reorders the unmasking. The three components act at non-overlapping stages of a decoding step and compose freely with existing dMLLMs and caches. Across three dMLLMs and two caching backends, CoTA++ reduces the sample repetition rate of long responses from up to 99.6\% to at most 17.0\%, recovers most of the accuracy lost to caching on nine benchmarks, and keeps the speedup of caching at under 15\% overhead, making approximate caching reliable for dMLLMs.
items.title: CoTA++: Understanding the Repeat Curse in dMLLMs from an Information Flow Perspective

items.summary: Student-built load banks used in undergraduate electrical machines laboratories typically derive rotor speed from a slotted-disc tachometer whose pulse train is quantised by a fixed sampling clock, and the resulting slip estimate feeds directly into the torque-speed curve that students report. the present analysis treats the slip estimator as a formal object and derives its sampling distribution under a declared measurement model in which the tachometer quantisation interval is the dominant error source. The slip estimator is biased, that the bias is a function of the ratio of quantisation interval to synchronous period, and that the bias propagates into the torque-speed curve as a systematic displacement of the pull-out region rather than as random scatter. A replication-based evaluation was conducted: 600 data sets of N = 500 were drawn from a declared data-generating process (intercept 12.0, exposure 0.42, group -3.1, severity 1.35, error SD 4.2), and the ordinary least squares estimator was characterised under the stated process. The estimated bias for the intercept was -0.02315 and for the exposure coefficient 0.00064; the root mean squared errors were 0.88484 and 0.01581 respectively; empirical coverage of the nominal 95% confidence intervals was 1.0 for both parameters. The results indicate that the estimator is essentially unbiased for the slope but that the intercept carries a small negative displacement, and that the quantisation mechanism identified analytically is consistent with the direction and magnitude of the observed intercept bias. The stroboscopic benchmark should be reported alongside the torque-speed curve so that the slip bias is visible to the student and to the assessor.

items.summary: This repository provides the reproducible analysis materials accompanying the research article “Bitcoin and Sovereign Reserve Management: Portfolio Allocation, Model Sensitivity, and Downside Risk.” The study examines the sensitivity of Bitcoin allocations within a sovereign reserve-related portfolio framework, with particular emphasis on measurement consistency, model specification, allocation stability and downside risk. The empirical framework combines U.S. official reserve positions, Treasury gold holdings valued at market prices, and Bitcoin market-price observations. The principal estimation period covers April 2016 to July 2026, comprising 124 consecutive monthly changes. An extended historical sample beginning in January 2013 is used for sensitivity analysis. The analysis applies a Black–Litterman allocation framework with explicit budget constraints and alternative portfolio specifications. The reproducibility framework covers baseline portfolio estimation, alternative Bitcoin views and confidence levels, long-only allocation constraints, covariance sensitivity, rolling-window estimation, joint stationary bootstrap resampling and historical and hypothetical stress scenarios. Risk analysis includes volatility, Value at Risk (VaR95) and Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR95), with particular attention to adverse Bitcoin market conditions. The associated materials document the empirical procedures used to examine the sensitivity of estimated Bitcoin weights to data construction, estimation windows, covariance assumptions and portfolio constraints. They support independent examination of the quantitative results, robustness analyses, tables and figures reported in the accompanying research. The study uses publicly available financial and institutional data from the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, U.S. Treasury Fiscal Data, the World Bank and Coin Metrics. Associated research article: Bitcoin and Sovereign Reserve Management: Portfolio Allocation, Model Sensitivity, and Downside Risk. Research area: Financial Economics, Sovereign Reserve Management, Portfolio Optimization and Cryptocurrency Risk.

items.summary: AI agents increasingly use files and software tools to produce professional deliverables. Such work draws on materials, decisions, and feedback accumulated across assignments. We introduce OfficeTown, a generative simulation framework for professional organizations in which tasks and their context arise from continuing organizational work. From a natural-language description of an organization's purpose and activities, OfficeTown initializes an organization whose members coordinate work, delegate bounded assignments to assistant agents, and review their deliverables. Artifacts, decisions, and unresolved matters persist and shape subsequent work, while responsibilities and permissions determine what each member can see and do. We curate work requests, their context, and review feedback into executable resources for evaluation and learning. We construct OfficeTown Bench with 406 tasks and 4,836 evaluation criteria from 23 simulated organizations across eight professional domains, incorporating domain-expert feedback. Frontier-model evaluations reveal substantial remaining headroom. Supervised fine-tuning and on-policy distillation on OfficeTown data substantially improve Qwen3.5-9B on external professional-work benchmarks, including GDPval. Supplementary evaluations show that the principal--assistant harness achieves higher scores than the single- and multi-agent baselines tested. These results highlight the value of organizational simulation in generating work-grounded data and environments for the continued development of generalist agents.
items.title: OfficeTown: Generative Organizations for Evolving Agent Intelligence

items.summary: LLM-agent memory selection often uses retrieval rankings based on record relevance or individual influence. Such rankings cannot identify sufficient subsets under redundant or jointly necessary evidence. We study per-decision memory sufficiency: selecting a small subset that preserves full-memory behavior. To separate search error from model error, we introduce JointCoreBench, a benchmark with nine interaction families, six workflow domains, natural-language decisions, and exact sufficient-set oracles, and JointCore, a relevance cost-ordered group-deletion baseline that tests blocks before individual records. On 6,912 exact conditions, cost-ordered JointCore recovers a minimum-cost sufficient set in 100.0% of cases, reduces subset evaluations from 30.00 to 11.13 (62.9%), and achieves 87.8% active-memory savings. Across four 12B-70B model families and 432 tasks per model, its unweighted mean is 10.28 versus 16.00 model queries and 50.6% versus 43.1% minimum-cost recovery relative to cost aware singleton deletion. Both methods preserve full-memory behavior under the deterministic primary interface. Tests with physical deletion, UNKNOWN masks, PENDING sentinels, counterfactual values, and alternative labels identify interface dependent behavior. JointCore is an efficient benchmark baseline; the study does not establish deployment-ready memory compression.
items.title: Beyond Marginal Influence: Interaction-Aware Memory Selection for LLM Agents

items.summary: Reproducible and analytically robust research findings are essential to scientific progress, but evaluating these properties typically requires costly manual effort. We investigate whether LLM agents can help automate reproduction and robustness analysis, using a medical case study grounded in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database, a widely used U.S. cancer registry underlying tens of thousands of published studies. First, we introduce SEER-Repro, a benchmark of 20 published SEER-based papers together with the data and resources required to reproduce their findings. Second, we create an AI agent that successfully reproduces 77.4% of 2,190 atomic claims, while providing executable baselines for further analysis. Third, we develop an agentic analysis pipeline to test the robustness of the medical findings by identifying analytical choices underlying each finding, proposing defensible alternatives, and rerunning the analysis to determine whether those choices affect the conclusion. Across published papers in SEER-Repro, our pipeline identifies potentially consequential analytical choices in 9.5% of fully reproduced findings and flags them for expert review. These results show how LLM agents can support scientific review by reproducing findings, systematically testing their robustness, and directing expert attention toward potentially consequential analytical choices.
items.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery

items.summary: In autonomous driving, perceiving surrounding objects is not enough: failing to understand how they move and interact over time can lead to dangerous decisions. Evaluating vision-language models (VLMs) therefore requires testing whether they connect past spatial observations to future consequences. Yet existing benchmarks often assess edge cases through basic perception questions or test temporal understanding in simple scenarios, leaving complex spatiotemporal reasoning underexplored. We introduce STRIDE (SpatioTemporal Reasoning In Driving Edge Cases), an object-centric benchmark for long-tail, safety-critical driving scenarios. STRIDE covers six task families: spatial perception, spatial understanding, temporal memory, temporal extrapolation, trajectory prediction, and scene-context awareness. It pairs multiple-choice questions probing individual spatiotemporal judgments with related free-form visual question answering (VQA) requiring detailed scene explanations and justifications of driving decisions. We prioritize scenes with unusual object behaviors and complex traffic interactions, generate reference answers from structured dataset annotations through automated procedures, and use limited language-model assistance and human verification to ensure annotation quality. Across 12 proprietary, open-weight, and driving-specialized models, even the best performer, GPT-6-Astra, achieves only 43.4% average multiple-choice accuracy, versus an approximately 20% random-choice baseline. Further analysis reveals that strong performance in describing driving scenes does not necessarily translate to accurate safety-critical judgments, and that models struggle more with reconstructing object motion than recalling past positions. STRIDE thus exposes spatiotemporal driving limitations that aggregate VQA scores can conceal.
items.title: STRIDE: Evaluating Spatiotemporal Reasoning in Driving Edge Cases
